title: Sample every unit the claim covers
statement: Test a claim across everything it covers, every lesson, unit, standard, bank and population, not a showcase or convenient slice, reporting the share that holds and what went unchecked.
example: One model scored about 9 points lower on a single unit than across the whole course.
detail: An analytics note on the AP project flagged that its evaluation set sampled only three units of the course (`analytics.md`, line 156). A course check found one model at 59.0% on a single unit against 68.22% over the full course, about 9 points lower (`2026-05-27T2130Z_v80b_u1_baseline_course_check.md`, lines 24, 25 and 29), and a lab note found some standards failing systematically while others systematically passed (`system_improvement_brainstorm.md`, line 39). Everything a claim covers means every unit, standard, course, code path, item bank and learner population. Check hardest where the subject is least documented.
against: The single-unit result rests on one seed of 100 items (`2026-05-27T2130Z_v80b_u1_baseline_course_check.md`, line 7). No per-course failure rates are given, and the fact gap is offered only as a partial cause: "This partially explains why APWH factual_accuracy failures are more common than APUSH failures." (`icloud-work/ML learnings/knowledge_and_rag_pipeline.md`, line 217). The weaker memory for those courses is asserted, not measured (`icloud-work/ML learnings/what_is_ap_and_why_it_matters.md`, line 99). Even a full simulation is not field evidence: if the Rasch model is misspecified, all simulation results overestimate actual field performance (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`). The bias sat in the running estimate, not in the score the engine reports. The same audit's finding taxonomy counts 3 of 18 lessons, the reviewed one plus two (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`), where the skill file and the gradual-release dimension say 1 of 18; on either count most lessons lacked it.

Why 28 units matters: a system that performs well on APUSH but poorly on APWH/APEURO is not production-ready. The 97% target is across ALL 28 units, not just the most-trained ones.

**The APWH/APEURO challenge:** These courses have less internet training data than US history. The model's parametric memory is weaker for World and European history → more hallucination risk → factual_accuracy harder to achieve.

**Coverage gaps:** Some units have more facts than others. APUSH tends to have 150-300 facts per unit; APWH and APEURO units may have 100-200. This means APWH/APEURO questions have slightly less curriculum grounding. This partially explains why APWH factual_accuracy failures are more common than APUSH failures.

The most relevant finding: **"Fine Tuning vs. RAG for Less Popular Knowledge"** (SIGIR-AP 2024) showed that RAG surpasses fine-tuning by a large margin specifically for rare or less popular factual knowledge. AP history content includes many obscure primary source documents, minor historical figures, and precise dates — exactly the type of content where parametric knowledge is unreliable in any model under 100B+ parameters.

Existing source/native evidence is extensive but representative; it cannot silently waive unexecuted cells or classify them as human judgment.
One excellent lesson proves only that lesson and explicitly exercised shared surfaces.
A claim about "all 55 lessons" verified by opening 2 of them is a sampling gap, not verification.
A sample can illustrate; it cannot establish 55-lesson consistency or progression.
Never extrapolate one inspected lesson to unchecked lessons.

**Simulation scope.** The initial simulations recorded in the per-simulation sections below were run on a Grade-3-configured 630-item bank, with true ability drawn from a G3 fall prior N(−1.5, 1.0), and used a closed-form Fisher-information selector rather than the full production shadow-test path.
